clue.text: The Circle Line speculation?

parts.note: taken as written
a circle is the shape of the letter O
RY, short for railway, is a line in crosswords

explanation.surface: A London Underground route, the Circle Line, offered as a guess.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, so the surface reads as one unit; split it into three words, each giving its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea put forward without proof, which is what a speculation is.

clue.text: Novice incline to follow this Austrian climber?

indicators.note: the word for incline comes after the word for novice

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner
to lean is to incline

explanation.surface: A beginner set to follow an Austrian mountaineer up the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' sets the incline after the novice. Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria, so its natives are pictured as mountain people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Tyrol comes from Alpine country, so a mountaineer is the natural picture.

clue.text: Projector has to manage with mince-pies

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the letters of the word beside it are scrambled

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: A projector has to make do with Christmas mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of the festive mince pies, but it is the instruction to chop up the letters of 'pies'.
explanation.definitionFit: An episcope is an optical device that throws an image of an opaque object onto a screen.

clue.text: Portuguese coins buried in Treasure Island

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the two words, as treasure is buried

explanation.surface: Coins buried in Stevenson's Treasure Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' points to the run across treasurE ISland.
explanation.definitionFit: Reis were old Portuguese money units, plural of real.

clue.text: Mishap puts insurance department heads in stress

indicators.note: the head letters go inside the word for stress, so in marks a container here

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent

indicators.note: heads means take the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: An office mishap puts the leaders of the insurance department under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' gives I and D, which 'in' places inside ACCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unplanned unfortunate event, the same as a mishap.

clue.text: Cartoon's vein is unusual, making it this sort of piece?

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of the words before are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: An art critic notes that a cartoon's unusual streak makes it a talking point.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Cartoon's is a letter of the fodder, CARTOONS plus VEIN, which 'unusual' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation piece is an object that gets people talking, or a genre painting of a group.

clue.text: 1. in Greece, for Whit

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's ninth letter matches our I, and a jot or tiny amount is a whit.

clue.text: Metropolitan record chief

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
arch means chief, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: A city's chief record keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: A metropolitan is a senior bishop in the Orthodox Church, not a city dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: An eparch is a senior bishop in the Eastern Orthodox Church, the rank of a metropolitan.

clue.text: After putting, it is the other half of the game-winning?

definitions.text: After putting, it is the other half of the game

explanation.definitionFit: Put and take is a gambling game with a spinning top, and taking a prize means winning it.

clue.text: This fruit is dry, yet is in downpour

indicators.note: the second is goes inside the word for downpour, so in marks the container

parts.note: a downpour is heavy rain

explanation.surface: A complaint that the fruit stays dry even in a rainstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a raisin is a fruit that has been dried. 'in' places the second 'is' within the word for downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a grape that has been dried, a fruit sold in dry form.

clue.text: Obsessed with single theme, like monotonous record

explanation.definitionFit: A one-track mind fixes on a single subject, and a record with only one song repeats itself monotonously.

clue.text: Piano recital has splendid support

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below, so the word for splendid comes after

parts.note: a recital is a concert
grand means splendid

explanation.surface: A piano recital is backed by excellent sponsorship.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'support' puts GRAND under CONCERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert grand is the largest grand piano, built for performance halls.

clue.text: Rugby forward's tuft of hair

explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a lock is a second-row forward, and a lock is also a curl or strand of hair.

clue.text: Word processor for the treasury?

parts.note: not a computer program but the man who processed words into his famous Thesaurus, a word that means treasury

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the Thesaurus, Greek for treasure-house, by sorting words into groups.

clue.text: Medical investigation in study

explanation.definitionFit: A hospital scan images the inside of the body, and to scan something is to examine or read it closely.

clue.text: Lathered condition of retired person in outskirts of Surrey

indicators.note: the pensioner goes inside the edge letters, so in marks the container
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of Surrey

parts.note: OAP, old age pensioner, is a retired person

explanation.surface: The state of a pensioner living on the edge of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives S and Y, the first and last letters of Surrey, and 'in' puts OAP between them. Surrey is a county near London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in suds or foam is lathered.

clue.text: Precious stone, best from beginning to end

parts.note: top means best
the alphabet runs from A to Z, its beginning to its end

explanation.surface: A gem that is the finest through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from beginning to end' is A to Z, the whole alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a gem, often yellow, cut for jewellery.

clue.text: It could help chap shoot par, if controlled

definitions.text: It could help chap shoot par, if controlled

indicators.note: letters that are controlled are steered into order, so the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Golf advice: a man could make par if he kept a particular stroke under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if controlled' rearranges CHAP SHOOT PAR; the whole clue also describes the golf stroke played onto the green.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an approach shot is the stroke aimed at the green, and a good one helps a player make par.

clue.text: O.for this sort of letter

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape, and a mailing sent to many people bears the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A round letter of the alphabet and a mass-mailed notice share the same adjective.

clue.text: Describing me, retired i.e. rust-affected?

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of me, i.e. and rust are changed in order

parts.note: the letters of i.e. are used without the dots

explanation.surface: An old professor describes himself as retired and getting rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges ME, IE and RUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor who has stepped down but keeps the title as an honour.

clue.text: Medium chance of success in it?

definitions.text: Medium chance of success in it?

parts.words: Medium chance of success in it?
parts.note: reads as a modest probability of success, but a medium is a person said to contact the dead, and the belief they practise is meant

explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualism is the belief in contacting the dead, practised through mediums at seances.

clue.text: Deck-games etc.,left on board

indicators.note: on board means inside the ship, so the word for left sits within it

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a vessel one goes on board
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Games played on deck after leaving harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works with 'board': being on board a steamship is being inside it, so the word for left sits within the ship's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits and shuffleboard are games and athletic pastimes, played on a ship's deck.

clue.text: Crazy affair in the grass

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters of affair are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mad love affair conducted in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges AFFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is a palm fibre that looks like dried straw, used for weaving and tying plants.

clue.text: Quiet ballad in 29, for example

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
a lay is a narrative song or ballad

explanation.surface: A soft ballad sung within another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is HAMLET, Shakespeare's tragedy, so the answer is the kind of work it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a stage drama, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Retired soldier has WC fitted in "Bleak House"

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
WC, water closet, is a loo

explanation.surface: An old soldier has a toilet installed in a house named after Dickens's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns GI into IG. Bleak House is a Dickens novel, but here it means a cold, bare home of snow blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dwelling built of snow, a chilly and spartan home.

clue.text: Cliff and Mark

explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky outcrop in northern England, and also the mark left by a healed wound.

clue.text: Table Mountain-see me at South Africa

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit Table Mountain in Cape Town.
explanation.walkthrough: Table Mountain is a real flat-topped peak in South Africa, but here it means any flat-topped hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a steep-sided, flat-topped hill, shaped like a table.

clue.text: Shoot the river

explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to shoot forward fast, and the Dart is a river in Devon, England.

clue.text: Who needs foresight? Sack merchant!

parts.note: to rifle is to ransack or plunder, as to sack does
merchant is slang for a person given to an activity, as in speed merchant, so a man

explanation.surface: A question about planning ahead, answered by a dealer in sacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The foresight is the front sight on a gun barrel, not prudence; a sack merchant is one who rifles.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier armed with a rifle aims with its foresight, the sight near the muzzle.

clue.text: His play? Improbably!

parts.note: the tragedy bears the prince's name, so it is his play, yet he hardly wrote it, Shakespeare did

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy is named after its Danish prince, so the drama is in name his.

clue.text: Out of port for home counties prizes

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
prizes are awards

explanation.surface: Prizes won by the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading seawards is going towards open water, away from the harbour.

clue.text: Large bills used, reputedly, with their deliveries

definitions.text: Large bills used, reputedly, with their deliveries

parts.words: Large bills used, reputedly, with their deliveries
parts.note: reads as hefty invoices for delivered goods, but the bills are beaks, and folklore says these birds deliver babies

explanation.definitionFit: Storks are long-beaked wading birds, said in folk tales to bring newborn babies.
